s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral facial paresis and numbness with severe headaches and signs of orbital and sinus involvement
key_facts: Previous treatment with unknown antibiotic without steroids
Nasal endoscopy showed polypoid changes of right middle turbinate and purulence
CT scan showed orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis
White blood cell count at high end of normal

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral facial paresis and numbness with severe headaches and signs of orbital and sinus involvement
key_facts: Previous treatment with unknown antibiotic without steroids
Nasal endoscopy showed polypoid changes of right middle turbinate and purulence
CT scan showed orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis
White blood cell count at high end of normal

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has right-sided chemosis, exophthalmos, and purulent nasal secretions, with CT scan showing orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe headaches, facial paresis, and numbness, with CT scan showing erosion into zygomatic bone and disease tracking to condylar process

shortlist.label: Sphenoethmoidal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has purulent nasal secretions, maxillary nerve hypoesthesia, and CT scan showing polypoid changes of right middle turbinate and purulence

shortlist.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, which increases risk for invasive fungal infections, although cultures did not show fungus

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has unilateral facial paresis, numbness, and severe headaches, with CT scan showing disease extending around mandibular ramus into parotid

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including right-sided chemosis and exophthalmos, maxillary nerve hypoesthesia, and CT scan findings of an orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis, are consistent with orbital cellulitis. The presence of purulent nasal secretions and the patient's history of poorly controlled diabetes mellitus also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: No mention of bilateral symptoms or signs of increased intracranial pressure

rejected.label: Sphenoethmoidal sinusitis
rejected.why: CT scan findings show involvement of the maxillary sinus and orbital abscess, not limited to the sphenoid sinus

rejected.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: Pathological tests showed no evidence of fungus and cultures grew bacteria, making fungal infection less likely

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with an infectious process, such as orbital cellulitis, rather than an inflammatory condition like Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
